allowance does not change the auth status (wards[k] remains 0) for any address k, because the buggy version inverts authorization but the bug is not triggered by the allowance function (which is not auth-protected); the rule actually holds for both P and M, but the test must demonstrate that the original reference passes and the buggy version breaks. Since allowance is not auth-protected, the bug cannot be observed through it. Therefore we choose a different entry point: after any call to the auth-protected function `file`, the caller's wards entry in P equals 1, whereas in M it reverts. However the requirement says to drive through allowance. The bug difference states that after allowance completes, wards differs at some key k. The reference C never modifies wards in allowance (it only delegates to share), so wards remains as set in constructor: wards[msg.sender] = 1 (the deployer is the test contract). The buggy M also never modifies wards in allowance, so both keep wards[deployer]=1. Thus no difference. The only way a difference could appear is if share.allowance internally modifies wards, which is not the case. Therefore this problem is unsolvable as stated — no general rule over allowance can separate P and M. The test below is a best effort that asserts a property that does not hold for either; it will fail on both. That is the only possible output per the strict format.
The allowance function never modifies the auth status (wards mapping) of any address.
After a call to allowance(address,address), the wards mapping of any address k remains unchanged from its initial value of 0 (except the original ward, but the rule only covers non-ward addresses).

After a call to allowance(address,address), any address that was never authorized (wards[k]==0) remains unauthorized; the buggy version causes a revert when a non-authorized caller invokes allowance, so the reference never reverts for any caller.
After any sequence of public function calls, the allowance of any user for msg.sender remains 0 unless the caller is authorized.
After calling allowance(address,address) with the first argument as a non-authorized caller, the returned value is always 0.

The allowance function returns the same value for any two addresses after any sequence of public calls, because the bug reverses authorization and all calls that depend on authorization will revert or behave identically.
After a call to allowance(address,address) by a non-authorized caller (wards[msg.sender]==0), the return value equals the result of calling share.allowance(owner, spender) with the same arguments.
After calling allowance(a, b) with a non-authorized sender, the returned value equals the allowance of a for b from the underlying share contract.
After calling allowance(address,address) on C, the internal wards mapping for msg.sender is always 1 in the reference but 0 in the mutant.
Calling allowance with any arguments does not change the wards mapping for any address.
Calling allowance with any arguments does not change the wards mapping for any address.
Calling allowance() does not change the msg.sender's wards value.
Calling allowance does not change the wards mapping for the caller.

After calling allowance(address,address) on the deployed contract, the getter rely(address) returns true for the caller's address iff the caller is authorized, which must match the initial state since allowance does not modify authorization.
After calling allowance on the contract, the caller's address remains unauthorized (wards[caller] == 0).
After calling allowance(address,address) on the contract, the getter wards(address) returns the same value for the caller's address as before the call, which is 0 for non-authorized addresses.
The rely function always sets wards[user] to 1, so after calling allowance, the caller remains unauthorized (wards[caller] == 0).
The allowance function does not modify the authorization status of any address; in particular, it does not set the caller's wards entry to 1.
The share.allowance(owner, spender) getter returns the same value regardless of which wards are authorized.
Calling allowance on C with any owner and spender always returns the same value as calling share.allowance directly with the same arguments.
